981.explanation: In careful writing, start a sentence with The one that… or The ones that… to build up to the important information, which comes after is or are. You pick one thing out of many and put it in focus.
examples: The one that impressed me most was the carnival.
The ones that he preferred were adventure stories.
The one that will really help is better education.

uk.explanation: У ретельному письмі речення можна почати з The one that… або The ones that…, щоб підвести до головної інформації, яка йде після is або are. Ви вибираєте одну річ із багатьох і ставите її у фокус.

987.explanation: Put an adjective straight after something or anything to say what kind of thing you mean: something new, anything wrong. The adjective comes after the pronoun, not before it.
examples: I need something new to wear.
I didn't find anything wrong.
Let's do something different this weekend.

uk.explanation: Прикметник одразу після something або anything уточнює, яку саме річ ви маєте на увазі: something new, anything wrong. Прикметник стоїть після займенника, а не перед ним.

988.explanation: Put a to-infinitive after something or anything to say what the thing is for: something to drink, anything to wear.
examples: Please bring something to drink.
I didn't have anything to wear.
Have you got something to read?

uk.explanation: To-інфінітив після something або anything показує, для чого ця річ: something to drink, anything to wear.

990.explanation: Add or something at the end of a sentence to mean "this, or something similar". It is an informal way of not saying one exact thing.
examples: After the concert we can have a pizza or something.
Bring something to drink: juice, cola or something.
Is he ill or something?

uk.explanation: Or something у кінці речення означає «це або щось подібне». Це неофіційний спосіб не називати щось одне точно.

993.explanation: Put a word like absolutely, almost or nearly before an indefinite pronoun to make it stronger. Absolutely means 100%, and nearly or almost means just under 100%: absolutely anything, nearly everyone.
examples: You can find absolutely anything in that shop.
Nearly everyone I know works at a computer.
Almost nobody came to the meeting.

uk.explanation: Слово на кшталт absolutely, almost чи nearly перед неозначеним займенником підсилює його. Absolutely означає 100%, а nearly чи almost — трохи менше за 100%: absolutely anything, nearly everyone.

995.explanation: Start a sentence with something, everything or anything + a relative clause to build a longer subject. This puts the idea in focus before you say what it is. It is more formal and common in writing: Something that I like is…
examples: Something that I really like is the teachers.
Everything that I believed changed.
Anything that helps you practise English is useful.

uk.explanation: Почніть речення з something, everything або anything + підрядне речення, щоб утворити довший підмет. Так думка опиняється у фокусі ще до того, як ви скажете, що це. Це офіційніше й поширене на письмі: Something that I like is…

996.explanation: Use expressions like or something, or anything like that and or somewhere else to talk about things in a vague way. They mean "this, or something similar" and are common in speaking.
examples: Is it a cold or anything like that?
We could plant trees here, or somewhere else.
She's a teacher or something like that.

uk.explanation: Вирази на кшталт or something, or anything like that та or somewhere else допомагають говорити про речі нечітко. Вони означають «це або щось подібне» й поширені в усному мовленні.

997.explanation: Use anything + a relative clause or other words after it as a long subject, to put the idea in focus. The verb is singular: Anything that… is…
examples: Anything that gets you speaking English is useful.
Anything else can be sent by email.
Anything you say now will be remembered.

uk.explanation: Anything + підрядне речення або інші слова після нього може бути довгим підметом, що ставить думку у фокус. Дієслово в однині: Anything that… is…

998.explanation: Anything can start a clause with if there is left out: Anything you need, ask me = If there is anything you need, ask me. The main clause then follows after a comma.
examples: Anything else you need, ask Sarah.
Anything you want to know, just call me.
Anything you don't understand, write it down.

uk.explanation: Anything може починати частину речення, в якій пропущено if there is: Anything you need, ask me = If there is anything you need, ask me. Потім після коми йде головне речення.

999.explanation: Use you to talk about people in general, not only the person you are speaking to. It is normal in speaking and informal writing, often with can, can't, need to or have to.
examples: You can't park here after 8 am.
If you want to visit China, you need a visa.
With this phone you can take great pictures.

uk.explanation: You уживаємо, щоб говорити про людей загалом, а не лише про співрозмовника. Це звично в усному мовленні й неофіційному письмі, часто з can, can't, need to або have to.

1000.explanation: One means the same as general you, but it is formal. Use it in essays, formal letters and speeches. Keep using one in the sentence: one's, oneself.
examples: One should always read a contract before signing it.
One must look after one's health.
In this city, one sees cats everywhere.

uk.explanation: One означає те саме, що you у значенні «будь-хто», але звучить офіційно. Уживайте його в есе, офіційних листах і промовах. Не змінюйте його в межах речення: one's, oneself.

1001.explanation: Use we and us to mean people in general when you want to include yourself. It is common in essays and discussions and sounds more personal than one. Some of us, many of us divide people into groups.
examples: We all know that being a writer is difficult.
Zoos give us a chance to understand nature.
Some of us find technology useful, while others don't.

uk.explanation: We та us уживаємо в значенні «люди загалом», коли хочемо включити й себе. Це поширено в есе та дискусіях і звучить особистіше, ніж one. Some of us, many of us ділять людей на групи.

1002.explanation: After someone, anyone, everyone or no one, use they, them or their to refer back to the person. We use it when we don't know, or it doesn't matter, if it is a man or a woman. They keeps a plural verb: they are, they have.
examples: Everyone has to bring their own lunch.
If anyone calls, tell them I'm out.
If someone doesn't like the film, they can leave.

uk.explanation: Після someone, anyone, everyone або no one уживаємо they, them чи their, щоб повернутися до цієї людини. Так роблять, коли не знаємо або неважливо, чоловік це чи жінка. Дієслово після they лишається в множині: they are, they have.

1003.explanation: To refer back to a noun like a student or a person when you don't know if it is a man or a woman, you can use he or she (him or her, his or her), or they. He or she is more formal and takes a singular verb. Using only he sounds old-fashioned today.
examples: If a student is ill, he or she must call the school.
A good doctor listens to his or her patients.
If a child is bored, they won't learn.

uk.explanation: Щоб повернутися до іменника на кшталт a student чи a person, коли не знаємо, чоловік це чи жінка, можна вжити he or she (him or her, his or her) або they. He or she офіційніше й потребує дієслова в однині. Лише he сьогодні звучить застаріло.

1005.explanation: One another means the same as each other: two or more people do the same thing to the other person. It goes after a verb or a preposition and sounds more formal, so it is more common in writing.
examples: Students and staff can meet one another here.
Since we last saw one another, much has changed.
Team members should respect one another's opinions.

uk.explanation: One another означає те саме, що each other: дві чи більше людей роблять одне одному те саме. Стоїть після дієслова або прийменника й звучить офіційніше, тому частіше трапляється на письмі.

1010.explanation: End a question with or something else to give a list of ideas but leave the choice open. Put commas between the options and or before the last one: A, B or something else?
examples: Shall we buy him a book, a CD or something else?
Do you want to go swimming or do something else?
Poetry, history or something else?

uk.explanation: Or something else у кінці запитання дає список ідей, але лишає вибір відкритим. Між варіантами ставте коми, а перед останнім — or: A, B or something else?

1012.explanation: Put or not at the end of a question instead of repeating it in the negative: Did he pass or not? It asks for a clear answer and can sound impatient or annoyed.
examples: Do you want to do it or not?
Do you agree with me or not?
Are you coming or not?

uk.explanation: Or not у кінці запитання замінює повторення цього ж запитання із запереченням: Did he pass or not? Воно вимагає чіткої відповіді й може звучати нетерпляче чи роздратовано.

1013.explanation: In essays and arguments, make the second option of an alternative question an extreme one: the opposite, a disaster, a waste of money. It is not a real question; it makes the reader doubt the first option.
examples: Is this new industry a blessing or the exact opposite?
Is this reform real progress or just a waste of money?
Is social media helping us or destroying us?

uk.explanation: В есе й аргументації другий варіант альтернативного запитання можна зробити крайнім: протилежністю, катастрофою, марнуванням грошей. Це не справжнє запитання; воно змушує читача засумніватися в першому варіанті.

1014.explanation: In an alternative question with two clauses, don't repeat the shared subject and modal in the second clause: Could you A or B? With maybe or perhaps + could, this is a polite way to suggest ideas in formal writing.
examples: Maybe you could hand out toys or show a movie?
Should I stay or go?
Perhaps you could extend the trip or add another visit?

uk.explanation: В альтернативному запитанні з двох частин спільний підмет і модальне дієслово в другій частині не повторюють: Could you A or B? Із maybe або perhaps + could це ввічливий спосіб запропонувати ідеї в офіційному письмі.

1020.explanation: In informal speaking and messages, add right? at the end of a sentence to check that something is true. It never changes, so it is easier than a full tag, but avoid it in formal writing.
examples: You are 14 years old, right?
You asked me for some help, right?
The film starts at eight, right?

uk.explanation: У неофіційній розмові й повідомленнях right? у кінці речення перевіряє, чи щось правда. Воно ніколи не змінюється, тож це простіше за повний tag, але в офіційному письмі його уникайте.

1021.explanation: Add a tag after an imperative to make an order or request softer and friendlier. The usual tag is will you?; would you? and can you? are common too. After Let's…, the tag is shall we?
examples: Pass me the salt, would you?
Don't be late, will you?
Let's check together, shall we?

uk.explanation: Tag після наказового речення робить наказ чи прохання м'якшим і дружнішим. Звичайний tag — will you?; would you? та can you? теж поширені. Після Let's… tag завжди shall we?

1028.explanation: Use Why don't we…? or Why don't you…? + verb to make a friendly suggestion or invitation, not to ask for a reason. The answer is agreement or refusal: Good idea!
examples: Why don't we watch a film?
Why don't you come with me?
You still have a headache. Why don't you see a doctor?

uk.explanation: Why don't we…? або Why don't you…? + дієслово вживаємо для дружньої пропозиції чи запрошення, а не щоб дізнатися причину. Відповідь — згода чи відмова: Good idea!

1031.explanation: In an essay, a talk or a story, ask a wh- question and then answer it yourself. Nobody is expected to reply: the question points the reader to your next idea. Use one to open a paragraph, not several in a row.
examples: So what makes a good present? The best presents are personal.
But what are the alternatives? The city has a good subway.
Why does this matter? Because it affects everyone.

uk.explanation: В есе, виступі чи оповіді можна поставити wh-запитання й самому на нього відповісти. Відповіді ні від кого не чекають: запитання спрямовує читача до наступної думки. Одним таким запитанням починайте абзац, а не кількома поспіль.

1041.explanation: Use a negative yes/no question when you already think the answer is yes and want the listener to agree: Isn't that great? Don't you think?
examples: It's funny! Don't you think?
Isn't that a great idea?
Wouldn't that be amazing?

uk.explanation: Заперечне запитання yes/no вживаємо, коли ви вже думаєте, що відповідь «так», і хочете, щоб співрозмовник погодився: Isn't that great? Don't you think?

1042.explanation: In formal writing and argument, keep not in full and put it after the subject: Do we not…?, Is it not…? This makes the question an emphatic point, not a real question.
examples: Do we not want our children to be happy?
Is it not too easy to blame the schools?
Should we not protect our forests?

uk.explanation: В офіційному письмі й аргументації not можна лишити повним і поставити після підмета: Do we not…?, Is it not…? Так запитання стає наголошеною думкою, а не справжнім запитанням.

1043.explanation: Use look forward to + noun or -ing form to say you feel happy about something that will happen. The to is a preposition, so never use the bare verb after it. It is common at the end of a letter.
examples: I'm looking forward to seeing you!
I look forward to hearing from you.
We're looking forward to the holidays.

uk.explanation: Look forward to + іменник або форма на -ing показує, що ви з нетерпінням чекаєте на щось. To тут — прийменник, тож після нього ніколи не ставте дієслово в початковій формі. Це поширено в кінці листа.

1081.explanation: Use would love + to-infinitive to say you really want to do something. It is stronger than would like. In speaking, would is usually short: I'd love to…
examples: I'd love to see your new flat.
I would love to go to the concert with you.
She'd love to visit Japan one day.

uk.explanation: Would love + to-інфінітив показує, що ви дуже хочете щось зробити. Це сильніше, ніж would like. В усному мовленні would зазвичай скорочують: I'd love to…

1084.explanation: Use would prefer + to-infinitive to say politely what you want to do, often instead of something else. In speaking, it is usually short: I'd prefer to…
examples: I would prefer to pay by card, if that's OK.
I'd prefer to stay at home tonight.
We'd prefer to meet in the afternoon.

uk.explanation: Would prefer + to-інфінітив увічливо показує, що ви хочете зробити, часто замість чогось іншого. В усному мовленні зазвичай скорочують: I'd prefer to…

1092.explanation: Use a verb of the senses like see, hear, watch or feel + object + -ing form to show an action already in progress, caught partway through: I heard someone shouting.
examples: I heard someone shouting in the street.
We watched the children playing in the park.
She felt the rain falling on her face.

uk.explanation: Дієслово сприйняття на кшталт see, hear, watch чи feel + додаток + форма на -ing показує дію, що вже триває і яку ви застали посередині: I heard someone shouting.

1093.explanation: Use a verb of the senses like see, hear, watch or feel + object + infinitive without to to show the whole action, from start to finish: I saw him cross the road.
examples: I saw him cross the road and go into the shop.
We heard the door close behind us.
She watched the plane take off and disappear.

uk.explanation: Дієслово сприйняття на кшталт see, hear, watch чи feel + додаток + інфінітив без to показує всю дію від початку до кінця: I saw him cross the road.

1094.explanation: Use would hate + to-infinitive to say strongly that you don't want something to happen. It often comes before see, think or lose: I would hate to see…
examples: We would hate to see all that work wasted.
I'd hate to lose my old photos.
I would hate to think that you were unhappy.

uk.explanation: Would hate + to-інфінітив рішуче показує, що ви не хочете, щоб щось сталося. Часто стоїть перед see, think або lose: I would hate to see…

1107.explanation: Use if + present simple for a real condition: something true now, true every time, or very likely. The main clause uses the present simple, can, or an imperative.
examples: If I have free time, I read a book.
If you agree, we can go shopping after the film.
If you need help, call me.

uk.explanation: If + present simple вживаємо для реальної умови: того, що правда зараз, щоразу або дуже ймовірно. У головному реченні — present simple, can або наказовий спосіб.

1108.explanation: Short if-clauses like if you want, if you like or if you prefer make an instruction, offer or suggestion softer. They leave the choice to the listener, so you sound friendly.
examples: Bring some music if you want.
If you like, you can stay for dinner.
We can take the bus or, if you prefer, a taxi.

uk.explanation: Короткі if-речення на кшталт if you want, if you like чи if you prefer пом'якшують інструкцію, пропозицію чи пораду. Вони залишають вибір слухачеві, тому ви звучите дружньо.

1109.explanation: For a possible future situation and its likely result, use if + present simple and will in the main clause. This is the first conditional. Don't use will in the if-clause.
examples: If it rains, we'll stay at home.
Your parents will be happy if you visit them.
If we don't leave now, we won't catch the train.

uk.explanation: Для можливої ситуації в майбутньому та її ймовірного результату вживаємо if + present simple і will у головному реченні. Це first conditional. В if-реченні will не вживаємо.

1110.explanation: Use if + present simple with a modal verb in the main clause when the result is possible, not certain. Use can for a possibility or permission, may or might when you are less sure, and should for advice.
examples: If you come to Kyiv, you can stay with us.
If it rains tomorrow, the match might be cancelled.
If you feel ill, you should see a doctor.

uk.explanation: If + present simple з модальним дієсловом у головному реченні вживаємо, коли результат можливий, але не певний. Can — для можливості чи дозволу, may або might — коли ви менш упевнені, should — для поради.

1111.explanation: The if-clause can use the present continuous or going to for someone's plan. The main clause then usually gives advice with should or an imperative.
examples: If you are moving, you should think about it carefully.
If you're going to travel, choose your partner carefully.
If you are looking for a job, ask at the café.

uk.explanation: В if-реченні може стояти present continuous або going to, щоб говорити про чийсь план. Тоді головне речення зазвичай дає пораду з should або в наказовому способі.

1112.explanation: For an imagined situation, something unreal now or unlikely in the future, use if + past simple and would in the main clause. This is the second conditional. The past form does not mean past time here; it shows the situation is imagined.
examples: If I had more money, I would travel more.
It would be more fun if you came with us.
If you went on holiday, where would you go?

uk.explanation: Для уявної ситуації — нереальної зараз або малоймовірної в майбутньому — вживаємо if + past simple і would у головному реченні. Це second conditional. Минула форма тут не означає минулий час; вона показує, що ситуація уявна.

1113.explanation: If I were you + would is the usual way to give advice: you imagine yourself in the other person's place. In this fixed phrase, use were, not was.
examples: If I were you, I would take the job.
If I were you, I'd call her today.
I wouldn't worry about it if I were you.

uk.explanation: If I were you + would — звичайний спосіб дати пораду: ви уявляєте себе на місці іншої людини. У цьому сталому звороті вживаємо were, а не was.

1114.explanation: Unless means "except if" or "if … not". Use unless + present simple for the one situation in which the main clause is not true. The verb after unless is positive, because the negative idea is already in the word.
examples: I'll pay in cash unless you accept cards.
Unless you hurry, you'll be late.
We can't go in unless we have tickets.

uk.explanation: Unless означає «хіба що» або «якщо не». Unless + present simple вживаємо для єдиної ситуації, в якій головне речення неправдиве. Дієслово після unless стверджувальне, бо заперечення вже є в самому слові.

1115.explanation: Use if + past simple with could in the main clause to say what would be possible in an imagined situation. It is a gentle way to make a suggestion.
examples: If you wanted to go outside, we could go fishing.
If you arrived early, we could have lunch together.
We could buy a bigger flat if we had more money.

uk.explanation: If + past simple з could у головному реченні показує, що було б можливо в уявній ситуації. Це м'який спосіб щось запропонувати.

1116.explanation: To imagine a different past, something that did not happen, use if + past perfect and would have + past participle. This is the third conditional. It often shows regret or relief.
examples: If you had asked me, I would have helped.
If I hadn't missed the bus, I wouldn't have been late.
We would have won if we had played better.

uk.explanation: Щоб уявити інше минуле — те, чого не сталося, — вживаємо if + past perfect і would have + past participle. Це third conditional. Воно часто виражає жаль або полегшення.

1117.explanation: After a yes/no question, If not means "if the answer is no". It replaces a whole if-clause, so you don't repeat the question, and it usually offers another option.
examples: Is Friday OK for you? If not, call me.
Do you work on Sundays? If not, let's meet then.
Check if the shop is open. If not, try the market.

uk.explanation: Після загального питання If not означає «якщо відповідь — ні». Воно замінює все if-речення, тож питання не треба повторювати, і зазвичай пропонує інший варіант.

1118.explanation: After a yes/no question, If so means "if the answer is yes". It replaces a whole if-clause, so you don't need to repeat the question.
examples: Can I pay by card? If so, which cards do you take?
Are you free tonight? If so, let's go out.
Did you like the book? If so, I have another one.

uk.explanation: Після загального питання If so означає «якщо відповідь — так». Воно замінює все if-речення, тож питання не треба повторювати.

1119.explanation: As long as, provided (that) and providing (that) mean "only if": the main clause is true on this one condition. Like if, they take a present tense for a future condition. Provided sounds more formal.
examples: You can borrow my car as long as you drive carefully.
Provided you book early, you'll get a discount.
Providing we follow the plan, sales will increase.

uk.explanation: As long as, provided (that) і providing (that) означають «лише якщо»: головне речення правдиве тільки за цієї умови. Як і після if, для майбутньої умови після них вживаємо теперішній час. Provided звучить офіційніше.

1120.explanation: The third conditional can use other modal verbs instead of would: if + past perfect, then could have, might have or should have + past participle. Could have shows a lost possibility, and might have means you are not sure what would have happened.
examples: All this could have been avoided if we had planned better.
I might have agreed if you had asked nicely.
If she had studied, she could have passed.

uk.explanation: У third conditional замість would можна вжити інші модальні дієслова: if + past perfect, а далі could have, might have чи should have + past participle. Could have показує втрачену можливість, а might have — що ви не впевнені, що було б.

1122.explanation: If + should + base verb makes a condition sound less likely and more polite, like "if, by any chance". It is typical of formal letters, instructions and customer service.
examples: If you should have any questions, please contact us.
If you should get lost, call this number.
If the machine should stop, press the red button.

uk.explanation: If + should + base verb робить умову менш імовірною і ввічливішою, на зразок «якщо раптом». Це типово для офіційних листів, інструкцій і обслуговування клієнтів.

1124.explanation: In very formal English, you can drop if and put should before the subject: Should you + base verb. With would in the main clause, it talks about a possible future result, often in formal promises or warnings.
examples: Should we win the prize, we would build a new school.
Should you fail to pay, we would have to take action.
Should the plan change, I would let you know at once.

uk.explanation: У дуже офіційній англійській можна пропустити if і поставити should перед підметом: Should you + base verb. З would у головному реченні це говорить про можливий майбутній результат, часто в офіційних обіцянках чи попередженнях.

1125.explanation: In formal writing, you can drop if from a past imagined condition and put had before the subject: Had + subject + past participle. The main clause uses would have, could have or might have + past participle, and the meaning doesn't change.
examples: Had we known, we would have come earlier.
Had he been more careful, he could have avoided the accident.
Had I left on time, I might have caught the train.

uk.explanation: В офіційному письмі в уявній умові про минуле можна пропустити if і поставити had перед підметом: Had + subject + past participle. У головному реченні — would have, could have чи might have + past participle, а значення не змінюється.

1126.explanation: Were + subject + to-infinitive is a formal way to imagine an unlikely future situation. It means the same as if + past simple but sounds more distant and literary. The main clause usually has would.
examples: Were I to win the scholarship, I would study in Japan.
Were you to compare the two, you would see many similarities.
Were this plan to fail, we would lose everything.

uk.explanation: Were + subject + to-infinitive — офіційний спосіб уявити малоймовірну майбутню ситуацію. Він означає те саме, що if + past simple, але звучить віддаленіше й літературніше. У головному реченні зазвичай would.

1127.explanation: So long as, on condition that and in the event that are formal ways to introduce a condition. On condition that sets a strict condition, and in the event that means "if this happens". They work with past, present or future meaning.
examples: I was allowed out on condition that I was home by ten.
You can stay so long as you keep quiet.
In the event that the flight is cancelled, you'll get a refund.

uk.explanation: So long as, on condition that та in the event that — офіційні способи ввести умову. On condition that задає сувору умову, а in the event that означає «у разі, якщо це станеться». Вони вживаються щодо минулого, теперішнього чи майбутнього.

1128.explanation: Were it not for + noun phrase means "without this person or thing". It is a formal form of if it were not for, with if dropped and were moved to the front. Don't contract it: weren't it for is wrong.
examples: Were it not for your help, I would have failed.
Were it not for the rain, we would go for a walk.
Were it not for her parents, she could not study abroad.

uk.explanation: Were it not for + іменникова група означає «якби не ця людина чи річ». Це офіційна форма if it were not for, де if пропущено, а were винесено наперед. Не скорочуйте: weren't it for — помилка.

1129.explanation: If it weren't for (or if it were not for) + noun phrase means "without this person or thing". It says that one thing is the only reason the situation is how it is. With would have in the main clause, it talks about the past.
examples: If it weren't for my friends, I would feel lonely.
If it weren't for that boy, I would have failed the exam.
If it were not for the internet, I couldn't work from home.

uk.explanation: If it weren't for (або if it were not for) + іменникова група означає «якби не ця людина чи річ». Цей зворот каже, що саме ця річ — єдина причина, чому ситуація така. З would have у головному реченні він стосується минулого.

1130.explanation: If + subject + were + to-infinitive imagines an unlikely future situation in formal English. It keeps if, unlike the inverted form were I to. The main clause usually has would.
examples: If it were to rain, the concert would move indoors.
The project would need more money if it were to succeed.
If he were to resign, who would replace him?

uk.explanation: If + subject + were + to-infinitive в офіційній англійській уявляє малоймовірну майбутню ситуацію. На відміну від інвертованої форми were I to, тут if лишається. У головному реченні зазвичай would.

1131.explanation: Whether or not says that the condition doesn't change the result: it is true in both cases. At the start of a sentence, a whether or not clause can be the subject, especially in formal essays.
examples: Whether or not it rains, the match will go ahead.
Whether or not tourists should follow local customs is debatable.
It depends on them whether or not they go to university.

uk.explanation: Whether or not означає, що умова не змінює результату: він правдивий в обох випадках. На початку речення підрядне з whether or not може бути підметом, особливо в офіційних есе.

1132.explanation: Use as you know to remind the reader of something they already know before you say something new. It can start the sentence or go in the middle, between commas. It sounds polite and friendly.
examples: As you know, my parents are leaving for Spain tomorrow.
I can't come because, as you know, I live in England now.
As you know, the shop closes early on Sundays.

uk.explanation: As you know вживаємо, щоб нагадати читачеві те, що він уже знає, перш ніж сказати щось нове. Зворот може стояти на початку речення або в середині, між комами. Звучить ввічливо й дружньо.

1133.explanation: At the start of a sentence, So sums up what you have just said and moves on to what follows from it: a plan, a question or an apology. It is informal, good for emails to friends.
examples: I'll be free at three. So, I'll come at half past.
So, what do you think?
I have a dentist appointment. So, I'm sorry, but I can't come.

uk.explanation: На початку речення So підсумовує щойно сказане й переходить до того, що з цього випливає: плану, питання чи вибачення. Це неформальний варіант, добрий для листів друзям.

1134.explanation: When you have several reasons or steps, number them so the reader can follow. First of all or Firstly opens the list, Secondly and Thirdly continue it, and Finally or Lastly introduces the last point. Each one starts a sentence, followed by a comma.
examples: First of all, I must thank you for your letter.
Secondly, we need good materials.
Lastly, don't forget to bring your passport.

uk.explanation: Коли у вас кілька причин або кроків, пронумеруйте їх, щоб читачеві було легко стежити. First of all або Firstly відкриває перелік, Secondly і Thirdly продовжують його, а Finally або Lastly вводить останній пункт. Кожен починає речення, після нього кома.

1135.explanation: Discourse markers like however, on the other hand and in contrast start a sentence that says something different from the one before. On the one hand ... on the other hand compares two sides of a question. They are followed by a comma.
examples: The hotel was expensive. However, the rooms were beautiful.
On the other hand, a small school is quieter.
My old flat was dark. In contrast, this one is very bright.

uk.explanation: Дискурсивні маркери на кшталт however, on the other hand і in contrast починають речення, яке каже щось відмінне від попереднього. On the one hand ... on the other hand зіставляє дві сторони питання. Після них ставимо кому.

1136.explanation: Markers like in addition, moreover, what is more and besides add another point that supports the same idea. Moreover and in addition are more formal; what's more and besides are more personal. Each starts a new sentence, followed by a comma.
examples: The flat is cheap. In addition, it's near the station.
Besides, you're 18 now — you aren't a baby any more.
Moreover, the staff are very friendly.

uk.explanation: Маркери на кшталт in addition, moreover, what is more і besides додають ще один аргумент на підтримку тієї ж думки. Moreover і in addition — офіційніші, what's more і besides — більш особисті. Кожен починає нове речення, після нього кома.

1137.explanation: You see and the thing is introduce information the listener doesn't know yet, usually an explanation or the real reason for a problem. They are informal and sound like speech, so use them in messages to friends.
examples: I'd love to come. The thing is, I have an exam.
You see, the park is the only green place near us.
The thing is, I've lost my keys again.

uk.explanation: You see і the thing is вводять інформацію, якої співрозмовник ще не знає, — зазвичай пояснення або справжню причину проблеми. Вони неформальні й звучать як усне мовлення, тож вживайте їх у повідомленнях друзям.

1138.explanation: A stance adverb at the start of a sentence tells the reader how you feel about what follows: unfortunately for bad news, luckily for good news, surprisingly for something unexpected. Actually and in fact introduce the real situation. They are followed by a comma.
examples: We missed the last bus. Luckily, a friend drove us home.
Surprisingly, the suitcase was Lucy's.
Actually, I don't have much time to watch TV.

uk.explanation: Оцінний прислівник на початку речення підказує читачеві, як ви ставитеся до того, що далі: unfortunately — погана новина, luckily — добра, surprisingly — щось несподіване. Actually та in fact вводять реальний стан речей. Після них ставимо кому.

1139.explanation: Similarly, likewise and in the same way say that the next point is like the one before: the same idea in a new example. They start the sentence, followed by a comma, and are typical of essays and reports.
examples: Prices rose in the city. Similarly, rents went up in the suburbs.
Children need sleep. Likewise, adults need regular rest.
Letters show feelings. In the same way, diaries do.

uk.explanation: Similarly, likewise та in the same way показують, що наступна думка схожа на попередню: та сама ідея на новому прикладі. Вони стоять на початку речення, після них кома, і типові для есе та звітів.

1140.explanation: Formal texts often mark where they begin and end. To begin with and For a start introduce the first point of an argument. In conclusion and To sum up open the final paragraph, where you give your main point or final opinion.
examples: To begin with, I want to thank you all for coming.
For a start, the tickets are far too expensive.
In conclusion, zoos are not cruel if animals are well cared for.

uk.explanation: Офіційні тексти часто позначають свій початок і кінець. To begin with та For a start вводять перший аргумент. In conclusion і To sum up відкривають останній абзац, де ви подаєте головну думку або остаточну позицію.

1141.explanation: Markers like in summary, to sum up, in short and overall introduce a short summary of the main points. They start the sentence, followed by a comma. They are typical of the last part of essays and reports.
examples: In summary, most students are willing to help.
To sum up, both options have clear advantages.
In short, the project was a success.

uk.explanation: Маркери на кшталт in summary, to sum up, in short та overall вводять короткий підсумок головних думок. Вони стоять на початку речення, після них кома. Вони типові для останньої частини есе та звітів.

1142.explanation: In a long formal text, you can point back to something you have already written instead of repeating it: as mentioned above, as mentioned earlier, as shown above. As described below and see below point forward. There is no subject after as: the phrase is short for 'as I mentioned above'.
examples: As mentioned above, we could negotiate better contracts.
As mentioned earlier, I have already asked for information.
As shown in the table below, sales have risen.

uk.explanation: У довгому офіційному тексті можна послатися на вже написане, замість того щоб повторювати: as mentioned above, as mentioned earlier, as shown above. As described below і see below вказують на те, що буде далі. Після as немає підмета: зворот — це скорочення від «as I mentioned above».

1148.explanation: Use wonder + a wh- word or if + a clause to report a question you ask yourself in your head. The clause has statement order, and after wondered the tense usually moves back.
examples: I wondered what she had written.
I really wondered who he was.
I wonder if they will come tomorrow.

uk.explanation: Wonder + wh-слово або if + підрядне речення передає запитання, яке ви ставите собі подумки. У підрядному реченні прямий порядок слів, а після wondered час зазвичай зсувається в минуле.

1152.explanation: When you report what someone said about the future, will usually becomes would. If you report it later, time words change too: tomorrow → the next day, next week → the following week. If it is still in the future, you can keep will and tomorrow.
examples: He said he would call me the next day.
They told us the shop would open the following week.
She said she's coming tomorrow.

uk.explanation: Коли переказуєте чиїсь слова про майбутнє, will зазвичай стає would. Якщо переказуєте пізніше, змінюються й слова часу: tomorrow → the next day, next week → the following week. Якщо подія ще в майбутньому, will і tomorrow можна лишити.

1157.explanation: To report what a written text says, like an advert, a letter or a guidebook, use says in the present simple. The text still says it now, so the verb in the reported clause stays in the present too.
examples: The guidebook says that we can get there by train.
Your advert says that you are looking for helpers.
It says the hotel has a swimming pool.

uk.explanation: Щоб переказати, що написано в тексті — оголошенні, листі, путівнику, — уживайте says у present simple. Текст і досі це «каже», тому дієслово в переказаній частині теж лишається в теперішньому часі.

1158.explanation: Use I was wondering or I was thinking to show thinking as a process that went on for a while. After it, use a wh- clause or a wh- word + to-infinitive: I was wondering what had happened.
examples: We were wondering what had happened.
While he was thinking how to reply, Jenny smiled.
I was wondering where to go next.

uk.explanation: I was wondering або I was thinking показують мислення як процес, що тривав якийсь час. Після них ідуть wh-підрядне речення або wh-слово + to-інфінітив: I was wondering what had happened.

1159.explanation: When you report past words later, move the tense one step back: past simple or present perfect becomes past perfect. Time words change too: yesterday → the day before, last week → the previous week.
examples: She said that she had won the lottery.
We told her we had been at her house the day before.
He said he had left his phone in a café.

uk.explanation: Коли пізніше переказуєте слова про минуле, зсуньте час на крок назад: past simple чи present perfect стає past perfect. Слова часу теж змінюються: yesterday → the day before, last week → the previous week.

1160.explanation: Put a phrase like in the morning or in my country at the start of a sentence to set the scene first. The rest keeps normal order: subject, then verb. A comma after the phrase is common.
examples: In the morning, I go to the beach.
In my country, people eat a lot of rice.
After school, we play football in the park.

uk.explanation: Фразу на кшталт in the morning чи in my country можна поставити на початок речення, щоб спершу описати обставини. Решта речення має звичайний порядок: підмет, потім дієслово. Після такої фрази часто ставлять кому.

1161.explanation: Put an adverb like suddenly, quickly, here or outside at the start to make it stand out. In stories, Suddenly warns that something unexpected is coming. The subject and verb still follow in normal order.
examples: Suddenly, the door opened.
Outside, it was raining hard.
Quickly, I opened the letter and started to read.

uk.explanation: Прислівник на кшталт suddenly, quickly, here чи outside можна поставити на початок, щоб його виділити. В історіях Suddenly попереджає, що зараз станеться щось несподіване. Підмет і дієслово після нього стоять у звичайному порядку.

1162.explanation: Use It is / It's + adjective + that + clause to give your opinion first and the news after: It's great that you got the job. This sounds more natural than starting with That… In speech, that is often dropped.
examples: It's great that you have a new job!
It's important that you are happy.
It's sad that you have to move away.

uk.explanation: It is / It's + adjective + that + clause дає спершу вашу оцінку, а потім саму новину: It's great that you got the job. Це звучить природніше, ніж почати речення з That… В усному мовленні that часто пропускають.

1163.explanation: Use The reason (that) … or The place (which) … + clause as the subject, then be, then the thing you want to highlight: The reason I am writing is to… That or which is optional. After the reason … is, use that or to, not because.
examples: The reason I am writing is to ask about the course.
The place we liked most was the old harbour.
The reason I left is that the pay was low.

uk.explanation: The reason (that) … або The place (which) … + clause стає підметом, далі be, а потім те, що хочемо виділити: The reason I am writing is to… That чи which можна пропустити. Після the reason … is вживаємо that або to, а не because.

1164.explanation: Start with The thing / fact / point / problem / reason + is (that) to show what kind of information is coming, then give it: The problem is I'm always late. That is optional; without it, a comma is common.
examples: The problem is that I'm always late.
The point is, we don't have enough time.
The thing is, I don't really like parties.

uk.explanation: Почніть із The thing / fact / point / problem / reason + is (that), щоб показати, яка інформація буде далі, а потім назвіть її: The problem is I'm always late. That можна пропустити; без нього часто ставлять кому.

1165.explanation: Fixed expressions like All in all, All things considered, At the end of the day or When it comes down to it can open a sentence and tell the reader how to take it — as a summary or as what really matters. Put a comma after them.
examples: All in all, the trip was a great experience.
At the end of the day, it's your decision.
All things considered, I'd choose the third option.

uk.explanation: Сталі вирази на кшталт All in all, All things considered, At the end of the day чи When it comes down to it можуть відкривати речення й підказувати читачеві, як його сприймати — як підсумок чи як те, що зрештою найважливіше. Після них ставимо кому.

1166.explanation: In reports, proposals and instructions, an imperative like Note, Notice, See or Consider can point the reader to something important. It isn't really an order — it's a signpost that says look at this.
examples: Note the disadvantages of this plan.
Notice the difference in price between the two offers.
See the attached file for more details.

uk.explanation: У звітах, пропозиціях та інструкціях наказовий спосіб на кшталт Note, Notice, See чи Consider може звертати увагу читача на щось важливе. Це не зовсім наказ — це вказівник, що означає «зверніть на це увагу».

1167.explanation: Use What + subject + verb as the subject, then is / was, then the important new information: What we need is more time. The what-clause is not a question, so don't add do.
examples: What we need is a strong campaign.
What I love about this city is the food.
What tourists want is to see famous places.

uk.explanation: What + subject + verb стає підметом, далі is / was, а потім важлива нова інформація: What we need is more time. What-речення тут не питання, тому do не додаємо.

1168.explanation: A wh-clause can be a heading or title: Why I think this is a good idea, How we could save money. It tells the reader what the paragraph below will answer. It isn't a question: no auxiliary before the subject and no question mark.
examples: Why you should choose this event
How we could benefit from the changes
What I learned in my first year

uk.explanation: Wh-речення може бути заголовком: Why I think this is a good idea, How we could save money. Воно показує читачеві, на що відповість абзац нижче. Це не питання: допоміжного дієслова перед підметом і знака питання немає.

1169.explanation: In formal, academic or business writing, a short -ed clause like Compared to…, Based on… or Faced with… can open the sentence and set the frame for the main clause. It has no subject of its own, so it describes the subject of the main clause.
examples: Compared to other cities, Berlin is safe for cycling.
Based on this survey, we recommend longer opening hours.
Faced with rising costs, the company closed two shops.

uk.explanation: В офіційному, академічному чи діловому письмі коротке -ed речення на кшталт Compared to…, Based on… чи Faced with… може відкривати речення й задавати рамку для головного речення. Власного підмета в ньому немає, тож воно стосується підмета головного речення.

1170.explanation: Not a + noun at the start means not even one and is strongly emphatic, almost literary. Follow it with a (usually passive) verb, or, when the noun is the object, with an auxiliary before the subject: Not a word did she say.
examples: Not a word was spoken during the journey.
Not a sound could be heard in the house.
Not a scrap of remorse do they show.

uk.explanation: Not a + noun на початку речення означає «жодного» і звучить дуже емфатично, майже літературно. Після нього йде дієслово (зазвичай у пасиві) або, якщо іменник — додаток, допоміжне дієслово перед підметом: Not a word did she say.

1171.explanation: A clause starting with How, Why or Where can be the subject of a sentence, often followed by be: Where he had gone was a mystery. It is formal and typical of essays. The verb after the clause is always singular.
examples: How they influenced my life is hard to explain.
Where he had gone was a mystery.
Why people travel is an interesting question.

uk.explanation: Речення, що починається з How, Why чи Where, може бути підметом, часто з be після нього: Where he had gone was a mystery. Це офіційний стиль, типовий для есе. Дієслово після такого речення завжди в однині.

1172.explanation: Add an adjective before the noun in The thing / fact / point / problem is (that) to show your judgement too: the sad thing, the only problem, the strange thing. It can be in the past (was) when you tell a story.
examples: The only problem is that the rooms are small.
The strange thing was that nobody answered.
The sad fact is, many people can't afford it.

uk.explanation: Якщо додати прикметник перед іменником у The thing / fact / point / problem is (that), можна одразу показати й свою оцінку: the sad thing, the only problem, the strange thing. У розповіді вживається й минулий час (was).

1173.explanation: Use It is / It was + noun + who / that + clause to say this one and not anyone else: It was Paul who stole the money. Use who for people and that for things. Be stays singular, even with a plural noun.
examples: It was Paul who stole the money.
It is this silence that I love most.
It was the students who complained.

uk.explanation: It is / It was + noun + who / that + clause означає «саме цей, а не хтось інший»: It was Paul who stole the money. Who вживаємо для людей, that — для речей. Be лишається в однині, навіть з іменником у множині.

1174.explanation: For extra weight, you can put two fixed expressions one after another at the start of a sentence: All in all, taking everything into account, … Don't use more than two, or the sentence sounds like a speech.
examples: All in all, taking everything into account, I'd choose the park.
But all of a sudden, out of nowhere, a dog appeared.
What is more, in my opinion, the price is too high.

uk.explanation: Для більшої ваги можна поставити на початку речення два сталі вирази поспіль: All in all, taking everything into account, … Більше двох не варто, інакше речення звучить як промова.

1188.explanation: Use a negative question (Isn't it…?, Don't you…?) or a question tag (…, aren't you?) to ask the listener to agree, or to check something you think is true. The n't stays with the auxiliary.
examples: Isn't it a beautiful day?
You're free on Saturday, aren't you?
Don't you think it's too expensive?

uk.explanation: Заперечне питання (Isn't it…?, Don't you…?) або розділове питання (…, aren't you?) вживаємо, щоб попросити співрозмовника погодитися або перевірити те, що вважаємо правдою. N't лишається при допоміжному дієслові.

1192.explanation: Use the full form not instead of n't to stress the negative, or in formal writing: I do not agree. In speech, you say not strongly to make it clear.
examples: I do not want to hear that again.
This is not acceptable.
The results have not been published yet.

uk.explanation: Повну форму not замість n't вживаємо, щоб наголосити на запереченні, або в офіційному письмі: I do not agree. В усному мовленні not вимовляють з наголосом, щоб воно звучало чітко.

1193.explanation: For strong focus, put never at the start, then the auxiliary before the subject, like a question: Never have I seen such a film. It is dramatic and fairly formal; the normal version is I have never seen…
examples: Never have I seen such a beautiful place.
Never had I felt so tired.
Never did I think I would win.

uk.explanation: Для сильного наголосу never ставлять на початок, а потім допоміжне дієслово перед підметом, як у питанні: Never have I seen such a film. Це звучить драматично й досить офіційно; звичайний варіант — I have never seen…

1194.explanation: Use neither … nor to join two words, phrases or clauses and make both negative: not this and not that. The verb stays positive, because neither already makes the sentence negative.
examples: Neither you nor I would like that.
We can neither eat nor drink during lessons.
The hotel was neither clean nor cheap.

uk.explanation: Neither … nor поєднує два слова, фрази чи речення й робить заперечними обидва: ні це, ні те. Дієслово лишається стверджувальним, бо neither уже робить речення заперечним.

1198.explanation: For focus, put not only at the start, then an auxiliary (or do / does / did) before the subject: Not only did she win, but she also… The second part often has but … also.
examples: Not only was the hotel cheap, but it was also clean.
Not only do they sell books, they also sell coffee.
Not only did he forget, he also lied.

uk.explanation: Щоб наголосити, not only ставлять на початок, а потім допоміжне дієслово (або do / does / did) перед підметом: Not only did she win, but she also… Друга частина часто містить but … also.

1199.explanation: Put not before a stance adverb like necessarily, really, entirely or exactly to make a statement softer and less direct: That's not necessarily true. It sounds more polite than a plain negative.
examples: This is not necessarily a bad idea.
Cooking is not really my thing.
I'm not entirely sure about the date.

uk.explanation: Not перед прислівником на кшталт necessarily, really, entirely чи exactly робить твердження м'якшим і менш прямим: That's not necessarily true. Це звучить ввічливіше, ніж просте заперечення.

1200.explanation: In formal writing, especially reports and surveys, use (very) few + plural noun to mean not many people: Very few students agreed. Few without a has a negative meaning — almost none.
examples: Very few people speak English correctly.
Few students answered the survey.
Very few employees use the gym.

uk.explanation: В офіційному письмі, особливо у звітах та опитуваннях, (very) few + іменник у множині означає «небагато людей»: Very few students agreed. Few без a має заперечне значення — майже ніхто.

1201.explanation: Put whatsoever after no + noun, or after nothing / none, to mean not even a little: no interest whatsoever. It is strong and fairly formal.
examples: We have no experience whatsoever.
There is nothing whatsoever to worry about.
He showed no interest whatsoever in the job.

uk.explanation: Whatsoever після no + noun або після nothing / none означає «анітрохи, зовсім»: no interest whatsoever. Звучить сильно й досить офіційно.

1202.explanation: Not a (single) + noun at the start of a sentence means not even one. It is literary and dramatic, and is often followed by a passive: Not a single noise could be heard.
examples: Not a single noise could be heard from the rooms.
Not a single person was told about the plan.
Not a word was said about the accident.

uk.explanation: Not a (single) + noun на початку речення означає «жодного». Це звучить літературно й драматично, і далі часто йде пасив: Not a single noise could be heard.

1203.explanation: Add you after don't to make a command a strong warning or an angry telling-off: Don't you ever do that again! It is spoken and emotional, often with ever or in Don't you dare.
examples: Don't you ever do that again!
Don't you dare touch my phone!
Don't you talk to me like that!

uk.explanation: Якщо додати you після don't, наказ стає суворим попередженням або сердитим докором: Don't you ever do that again! Це усне й емоційне мовлення, часто з ever або у виразі Don't you dare.

1204.explanation: To add another negative point after a negative sentence, start with Neither or Nor, then the auxiliary (do, be, can…) before the subject: I don't like it. — Neither does she. In writing, Nor is it… adds another negative fact.
examples: I don't like horror films. — Neither do I.
We can't talk here. Nor is it possible to relax.
She didn't call, nor did she write.

uk.explanation: Щоб додати ще один заперечний пункт після заперечного речення, почніть із Neither або Nor, а далі допоміжне дієслово (do, be, can…) перед підметом: I don't like it. — Neither does she. На письмі Nor is it… додає ще один заперечний факт.

1205.explanation: Use in the least after a negative verb, or before an adjective in a negative sentence, to mean not at all: I'm not in the least worried. It is emphatic.
examples: She was not in the least interested.
It doesn't matter in the least.
I wasn't in the least surprised by the news.

uk.explanation: In the least після заперечного дієслова або перед прикметником у заперечному реченні означає «анітрохи»: I'm not in the least worried. Це емфатичний вираз.
